meta.description: Run predictions with a finetuned KERMT checkpoint on a SMILES-only CSV. The skill validates that the input ckpt has task FFN heads (refuses pretrain ckpts with a redirect to kermt-finetune), validates the CSV, prepares the data (clean + rdkit_2d features), then launches main.py predict inside the kermt container (blocking, minutes-scale).

recommendations.title: Add guidance for large batch inference failures
recommendations.problem: No guidance on handling memory exhaustion or partial failures when running inference on large datasets (thousands to millions of molecules)
recommendations.root_cause: Assumes batch size adjustment sufficient; doesn't address chunking strategy
recommendations.fix: Add to Common errors: 'OOM or CUDA out of memory → reduce --batch-size (try 16 or 8 for low VRAM). For very large CSVs (>100k molecules), consider splitting input into chunks and running inference separately on each, then concatenating predictions.'

recommendations.title: Document predictions.csv structure for downstream use
recommendations.problem: Step 7 mentions predictions.csv contains smiles + per-target columns but structure not fully specified
recommendations.fix: Expand Step 7: 'predictions.csv — one row per input molecule with columns: smiles (canonical), <target1>, <target2>, ... (predicted values for each task the model was finetuned on). Target column names match the original finetune CSV. Load with: pd.read_csv("predictions.csv")'

recommendations.title: Add idempotency statement for repeated inference
recommendations.problem: No explicit guidance on whether running inference multiple times with same inputs produces identical predictions
recommendations.root_cause: Determinism via --seed mentioned but not consolidated into idempotency guarantee
recommendations.fix: Add to Hard rules: 'Idempotency: inference is deterministic when --seed N is set (same checkpoint and CSV produce identical predictions across runs). Without --seed, minor stochastic variation may occur in featurization. Timestamped run directories prevent overwrites; outputs are reproducible via cmd_replay.'
